claims.text: David Ellison is the chief executive of the newly formed media conglomerate Skydance.
David Ellison acknowledged that Skydance has a good relationship with Donald Trump's administration.
David Ellison stated that Skydance leadership has not spoken to any political leader about news other than expressing a desire to be in the truth and trust business.
David Ellison stated that both CNN and CBS News will maintain complete editorial independence.
Mark Thompson informed staffers that he will remain as chief executive of CNN following the merger.
Skydance confirmed that Bari Weiss will remain in her role as editor-in-chief at CBS News.
David Ellison stated that most of the expected $6 billion in savings from the merger would not come from job losses.
Paramount Skydance completed its $110 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery on Tuesday to form Skydance.
Former Mattel chief Ynon Kreiz was appointed co-CEO of Skydance alongside David Ellison.
The merger settlement terms require Skydance to assemble an independent editorial oversight board for CNN and CBS News within 180 days.
Nielsen ratings showed viewership for 60 Minutes fell 21 percent during its season premiere compared to the prior year.
Skydance stock began trading under the ticker symbol SKYD on Tuesday and dropped 2.5 percent after opening.
The combined company Skydance carries $80 billion in debt following the deal.
Under the settlement agreement, Skydance must release 30 movies annually for the first two years and 32 movies annually for the remaining three years.
Skydance is required to release at least four independent films into cinemas each year under the settlement terms.
If Skydance fails to meet its movie quota, it could be forced to sell its 49 percent stake in Miramax.
A report by CVL Economics estimated the merger could eliminate roughly 4,500 direct film and TV jobs and cause $1.26 billion in lost wages over three years.
Warner Bros. Discovery shareholders will receive about $31 per share in cash under the merger agreement.
The Skydance transaction was backed by $47 billion in new equity led by the Ellison family, RedBird Capital, and sovereign wealth funds from Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Abu Dhabi.
DW reported that the takeover cost a total of around $81 billion, or almost $111 billion including Warner Bros. Discovery's debts.
Saint-Denis Mayor Bally Bagayoko was tear-gassed after shielding student protesters from riot police.
Hundreds of thousands of people marched across France as high school protests expanded to include parents, university students, and labor unions.
Police used tear gas in Paris and Marseille, water cannon in Rennes, and clashed with demonstrators in Lyon during nationwide school protests.
A French policeman was charged on Tuesday with violence after firing a tear gas grenade at close range at a 14-year-old high school student.
The French Interior Ministry estimated that 266,000 people demonstrated across France on Tuesday, including 56,000 in Paris.
French police detained nearly 500 people during nationwide demonstrations on Tuesday.
A 15-year-old boy lost his hand on Monday in an incident involving a police stun grenade during school protests.
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez stated that 715 police officers had been injured during the protest movement.
Classes were totally or partially suspended at 891 schools across France on Tuesday.
The French government's 2027 budget proposal aims to reduce the budget deficit from a projected 5.4 percent of economic output this year to 5 percent in 2027.
The French government aims to reduce state, local, and social spending by around €54 billion ($60.8 billion) compared with previous spending plans.
Belgian-born physicist Prof Francis Halzen was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for his leadership of the IceCube Neutrino Observatory at the South Pole.
Francis Halzen first presented his proposal for detecting neutrinos at the South Pole in 1988.
The IceCube Neutrino Observatory uses a cubic kilometer block of Antarctic ice embedded with light sensors to detect high-energy neutrinos.
Francis Halzen will receive a Nobel Prize amount of 12 million Swedish krona.
Francis Halzen is an 82-year-old professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in the United States.
Prof Mark Pearce serves as Chair of the Nobel Committee for Physics.
The Nobel Prize in medicine was awarded on Monday to three scientists for research using light to study brain activity.
The World Health Organization stated that the risk of an epidemic in Russia is low following the death of 28-year-old lab technician Darya Shipilova in Siberia.
WHO spokesperson Christian Lindmeier stated that the health risk was assessed as 'moderate to low' for Irkutsk, 'low' for Russia, and 'very low' for Europe.
WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus urged Russia to share timely and transparent information regarding Darya Shipilova's death.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called on Moscow to release more details regarding the death of the Russian lab technician.
Russian health agency Rospotrebnadzor offered to assist the US with infectious disease outbreaks, citing measles in three US states and a fatal plague case in New Mexico in June.
US President Donald Trump stated he scheduled a call to speak very soon with Russian President Vladimir Putin regarding the reported plague death.
Irkutsk Regional Governor Igor Kobzev stated that an inspection concluded Darya Shipilova died of pneumonia and that no microorganisms linked to her work were found in her samples.
The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention stated it is closely monitoring a suspected pneumonic plague outbreak in Russia.
Russian outlet People of Baikal reported that Darya Shipilova may have contracted pneumonic plague after a test tube broke at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute.
Testing on contacts of the deceased technician revealed two cases of COVID-19 and two cases of rhinovirus, but no dangerous infectious disease pathogens.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov urged the public not to listen to rumors and to rely solely on official health watchdog statements regarding the technician's death.
Flávio Bolsonaro won approximately 47 percent of the vote in the first round of Brazil's presidential election, compared to 45 percent for Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
Flávio Bolsonaro's Liberal Party secured the largest bloc of seats in Brazil's Senate.
A September Datafolha poll found 34 percent of Brazilians associated the Banco Master scandal with the political left, while 27 percent associated it with the right.
Defeated right-wing presidential candidates Ronaldo Caiado and Romeu Zema endorsed Flávio Bolsonaro for the presidential runoff.
Brazil's gross domestic product was approximately $2.28 trillion in 2025, representing about 31 percent of Latin America's economy.
Brazil accounted for 93 percent of global niobium production and roughly 17 percent of global iron ore production in 2024.
Four members of Jair Bolsonaro's family were elected to public office during Brazil's elections: his wife Michelle, sons Flávio and Carlos, and brother Renato.
Michelle Bolsonaro was elected to the Senate while caring for Jair Bolsonaro as he serves house arrest for attempting a coup.
Jair Renan Valle Bolsonaro was elected as a federal congressman.
Brazil's presidential runoff election between Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro is scheduled for 25 October.
US Vice President JD Vance stated that Iran must make a meaningful reduction in its nuclear enrichment capacity to satisfy US demands to end the war.
JD Vance questioned why Iran requires 60 percent enriched fuel if it does not intend to build a nuclear weapon.
JD Vance confirmed that the US is holding talks with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi.
Brent crude futures rose 93 cents to $101.51 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate crude rose 82 cents to $90.25.
US CENTCOM rejected reports from Iranian media claiming an American Navy MH-60R helicopter crashed in the Red Sea.
Donald Trump stated in Maryland that the war with Iran will end either in a 'nice way or not-so-nice way'.
During a campaign rally in Nebraska, Donald Trump suggested Iran could 'take out' Los Angeles or San Diego, calling it a small price to pay to keep the country safe.
California Governor Gavin Newsom called Donald Trump's rally remarks 'deranged' and 'dangerous'.
Republican congressional candidate Jim Desmond publicly rejected Trump's comments, stating that no American city is expendable.
San Diego County is home to roughly 250,000 military veterans, with defense spending accounting for 22 percent of its gross regional product.
Governor Gavin Newsom directed California's State Threat Assessment Center to monitor potential foreign security threats following Trump's comments.
White House Communications Director Steven Cheung stated Trump was asserting that US cities would have been threatened if a nuclear Iran had not been stopped.
Former German BND foreign intelligence chief August Hanning was arrested on Tuesday on suspicion of attempted treason, obtaining state secrets, and espionage.
Prosecutors accused former BND office manager Manfred D. of delivering approximately 2,000 confidential documents to August Hanning for money.
Der Spiegel reported that German investigators are pursuing potential links between August Hanning and an agent from Azerbaijan.
Documents allegedly leaked by Manfred D. included classified briefings on the Iranian nuclear program and the Russian military.
August Hanning was arrested in Bad Toelz-Wolfratshausen in southern Germany, while Manfred D. was arrested in Steinfurt.
Manfred D. served as chief of staff for August Hanning and several subsequent BND presidents from 2012 until 2026.
Evidence leading to August Hanning's espionage investigation was found during a search of his residence related to a custody case involving steakhouse heiress Christina Block.
August Hanning served as head of Germany's Federal Intelligence Service (BND) from 1998 to 2005.
German prosecutors alleged Hanning used classified intelligence to draft an analysis for an officer of a foreign intelligence service.
Kenya confirmed its first-ever Ebola death after a patient arrived in Nairobi from the Democratic Republic of Congo via Uganda.
Kenyan Health Minister Aden Duale stated the deceased patient tested positive for the rare Bundibugyo species of Ebola, which has no approved vaccine or specific treatment.
The patient died at 23:30 on Monday at an isolation facility in Nairobi and was buried on Tuesday following public health safety protocols.
Kenyan health authorities identified at least 28 contacts and are tracing 23 passengers and four crew members from the patient's flight.
The World Health Organization has recorded 4,114 deaths out of 8,544 cases in the current Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
Official figures as of October 2 recorded 4,082 deaths out of 8,463 confirmed Ebola cases in the DRC since May.
Médecins Sans Frontières reported that eastern North Kivu province in the DRC now accounts for 40 percent of all new Ebola cases nationwide.
Pro-government Homeland Shield Forces launched a large-scale military operation to retake the al-Waziiya district in Taiz governorate.
Saudi Arabia intercepted and destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile targeting the city of Khamis Mushait.
Attacks targeting King Abdullah bin Abdulaziz airport in Jazan and Najran airport in Saudi Arabia wounded three people.
Pakistan and Turkey agreed to activate deterrence measures under a mutual defense agreement with Saudi Arabia to deploy forces against Houthi attacks.
Yemeni pro-government forces announced they secured the Bab al-Mandeb Strait and captured the Red Sea city of Mokha.
Houthi spokesman Mohammed Abdul Salam rejected claims that the group lost Mokha or Bab al-Mandeb, calling them Saudi propaganda.
The Saudi-led military coalition stated its fighter jets destroyed 324 high-value Houthi targets during the offensive.
Houthi forces launched ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco oil facilities in Riyadh and Khurais.
Heavy fighting across Taiz province killed 34 Yemeni government soldiers and 39 Houthi fighters over a single day.
Houthi fighters cut the primary supply route linking the city of Taiz with the Yemeni government's interim capital of Aden.
Yemeni forces claimed to tighten control over the highest peak in the Jabal Habashi district of Taiz.
Saudi-backed government forces launched air strikes against Houthi positions as Jazan and Najran airports were struck.
